p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** This file defines *how* a tool writes into a file it does not own: the co-tenant law that bounds it to one delimited region, the marker design that makes that region findable by a deterministic scan, the well-formedness state machine that classifies a file before any mutation, the three verbs the tool is allowed (create / update / remove), and how two tools cohabit one file without ever colliding.

problem.title: The problem: a tool clobbering a shared file

p.MANY-TOOLS-WRITE-INTO-FILES-THEY-DO-NOT-: Many tools need to write into a file they did not create and do not solely own.

p.example-an-agent-framework-wants-a-line-: An agent framework wants a line in `CLAUDE.md`.

p.example-a-linter-drops-config-into-packa: A linter drops config into a shared `package.json`.

p.EACH-OF-THESE-FILES-ALREADY-CARRIES-OTHE: Each of these files already carries content from other parties — the user by hand, and often one or more *other* tools.

p.THE-NAIVE-IMPLEMENTATION-IS-A-WHOLE-FILE: The naive implementation is a whole-file rewrite: read a template, fill it in, `write()` the file.

p.IT-IS-EASY-AND-IT-IS-A-DATA-LOSS-EVENT: It is easy, and it is a **data-loss event**.

p.THE-FIRST-INSTALL-DESTROYS-EVERY-OTHER-T: The first install into any project with a non-trivial host file silently destroys every byte the user and every other tool put there — and it destroys precisely the file a person is most likely to have invested in by hand.

p.the-discipline-is-old-and-universal: The discipline that avoids this is old and universal: `ssh`, shell-rc installers, and countless config tools already use it.

p.THE-TOOL-OWNS-ONE-DELIMITED-MACHINE-FIND: The tool owns one small, clearly delimited, machine-findable region and never touches a byte outside it.

p.the-host-file-stops-being-the-tools-file: The host file stops being "the tool's file."

p.IT-BECOMES-A-SHARED-FILE-WITH-THE-TOOLS-: It becomes **a shared file with the tool's block in it**.

quote.THE-CO-TENANT-LAW: Own exactly one delimited block. Never touch a byte outside it.

p.A-GOOD-CO-TENANT-WRITES-INTO-ITS-OWN-PEN: A good co-tenant writes into its own pen and leaves the rest of the file to whoever else shares it. Stated operationally:

facts.TOOL-REWRITES-ONLY-BETWEEN-ITS-OWN-MARKE: The tool reads and rewrites only the content **between** its own opening and closing markers.
facts.EVERY-BYTE-OUTSIDE-THE-BLOCK-IS-PRESERVE: Every byte outside that block is another tenant's property, **preserved verbatim** across every operation the tool performs — install, update, uninstall, reconfigure.
facts.THE-TOOL-ASSUMES-IT-IS-NEVER-THE-ONLY-TE: The tool assumes it is **never the only tenant**. Even in an empty project today, a human or a second tool may share the file tomorrow.

p.the-same-rule-a-c-include-obeys: This is the same rule a C `#include` obeys: pulling in a dependency must never modify the including file's own authored content.

markers.title: Marker design

p.THE-BLOCK-IS-BOUNDED-BY-AN-OPENING-AND-A: The block is bounded by an opening marker and a closing marker, each alone on its own line.

td.fact: The marker string must not plausibly occur in host content. Namespace it with the tool's name — `# >>> toolname >>>`, `<toolname>`, `# BEGIN toolname`. A generic `# BEGIN` will collide.
Locatable by a plain line-anchored text scan — no format parser, no model. See the next section on why.
A distinct open and close, so a byte scan yields an unambiguous region, not a single sentinel whose end must be guessed.
The first line *inside* the block carries a do-not-edit notice, so a human reading the host file learns the region is managed without consulting docs.

p.a-worked-block-using-bare-tags: A worked block, using bare tags (chosen here because the primary reader is an LLM, to which a tag reads unambiguously):

markers.fence: <toolname> <!-- Generated by toolname — do not edit inside this block; it is rewritten on `toolname sync`. --> ... the managed body ... </toolname>

p.COMMENT-STYLE-MARKERS-SUIT-AN-RC-FILE-OR: Comment-style markers suit an rc file or ssh config equally well:

markers.fence: # >>> toolname managed block >>> # Do not edit between these markers; regenerated by `toolname apply`. export PATH="$PATH:/opt/toolname/bin" # <<< toolname managed block <<<

p.THE-MARKER-SYNTAX-IS-A-WIRE-FORMAT: The marker syntax is a wire format between your tool's past and future selves.

p.old-blocks-in-the-wild-still-carry-the-o: If you ever need to change it, old blocks in the wild still carry the old markers.

p.CARRY-A-VERSION-TOKEN-IN-THE-OPENING-MAR: Carry a small version token in the opening marker (`<toolname v=1>`) or in the notice line, so a future release can recognise and migrate a v1 block instead of appending a duplicate v2 one beside it.

p.DECIDE-THE-VERSION-BEFORE-THE-FIRST-RELE: Decide this before the first release — retrofitting a version onto an unversioned marker means one painful generation of heuristics.

p.THE-TOOL-CLASSIFIES-THE-HOST-FILE-BEFORE: Before writing, the tool classifies the host file by counting its own markers.

td.fact: Exactly one opener, then exactly one closer, in order
Update or remove the body between them.
Anything else — two+ of either marker, an opener with no closer, a closer with no opener, or a closer before its opener

p.A-MALFORMED-BLOCK-IS-ALWAYS-A-HUMANS-CAL: A malformed managed block is **always a human's call**: the tool never guesses which of two blocks is canonical, never deletes a stray marker, never auto-repairs.

p.IT-ABORTS-NAMES-THE-DEFECT-AND-WAITS: It aborts the whole operation, names the file and the exact defect, and waits.

p.auto-repair-rationale-pointer: The rationale is in [`rejected-designs.xml`](rejected-designs.xml#auto-repair): auto-repair destroys the evidence a human needs and may destroy user content that drifted into the wrong side of a marker.

p.EVERYTHING-THE-TOOL-DOES-IS-ONE-OF-THREE: Everything the tool does to the block is one of three operations.

facts.VERB-CREATE: **Create** — the file is *absent* of a block. Append the block at the **end of the file**, preceded by one blank line of separation. If the file itself does not exist, create it containing only the block. End-of-file is the humble default: the tool does not claim the attention-priority top of a shared file.
facts.VERB-UPDATE: **Update** — the file is *present*. Replace the content between the markers with freshly generated content. The markers themselves, and every byte outside them, are untouched. If the new body is byte-identical to the old, write nothing (§no-op).
facts.VERB-REMOVE: **Remove** — the file is *present* and the tool is uninstalling. Delete the block **and its separation** — the blank line the create step added — leaving the surrounding content byte-identical to what it was before the block ever existed. A remove that leaves a dangling blank line is a remove with a bug.

p.THE-TOOL-DECIDES-THE-POSITION-EXACTLY-ON: The tool decides the block's position **exactly once** — at create, appended to the end.

p.FROM-THEN-ON-THE-POSITION-IS-THE-USERS: From then on the position is the **user's**.

p.UPDATE-NEVER-RELOCATES-THE-MARKERS: Update rewrites the body and never relocates the markers; if the user moved the block to the top of the file, the tool splices it in place, wherever they put it.

p.honouring-position-lets-the-user-tune-th: Honouring that lets the user tune how strongly the block weighs: at the top of an instruction file it reads as a first, system-prompt-like instruction; at the bottom it is a sidecar.

p.THE-TOOL-SUPPLIES-A-DEFAULT-AND-NEVER-OV: The tool supplies a polite default and never overrides the choice.

plan-time.title: Classify at plan time, not mid-write

p.CLASSIFY-BEFORE-ANY-MUTATION-BEGINS: Run the absent / present / malformed classification **before** any mutation begins — in a planning pass that touches nothing.

p.a-half-applied-change-has-no-clean-state: A tool that discovers a malformed block halfway through a multi-file write has already half-applied its change: some files rewritten, one unwritable, no clean state to return to.

p.CLASSIFYING-UP-FRONT-FAILS-FAST-AND-CLEA: Classifying every target file up front means a malformed block fails the operation **fast and clean** — nothing is touched until every file is known to be writable.

p.THE-MUTATION-PHASE-SHOULD-NEVER-DISCOVER: The mutation phase should never discover a surprise.

p.DO-NOT-REWRITE-WHEN-THE-BODY-IS-BYTE-IDE: If the freshly generated body equals the existing body, **do not rewrite the file**.

p.an-unconditional-write-churns-mtime-and-: An unconditional write churns the file's mtime and, worse, produces a no-op diff in version control that a reviewer must read to confirm it changes nothing.

p.an-ignored-diff-is-where-a-real-change-h: A tool that writes on every invocation trains its users to ignore its diffs — and an ignored diff is where a real change hides.

p.COMPARE-THEN-WRITE-ONLY-ON-A-DIFFERENCE: Compare, then write only on a difference.

cohabitation.title: Multi-tool cohabitation

p.THE-LAW-SCALES-BECAUSE-EACH-TOOL-SCANS-F: The law scales to any number of tools because each tool scans only for **its own** markers.

p.two-tools-two-blocks-one-file: Two tools, two blocks, one file:

cohabitation.fence:
# Hand-written by the user — untouched by both tools. alias gs='git status'
<toolA> <!-- managed by toolA --> source /opt/toolA/env.sh </toolA>
# >>> toolB >>> # managed by toolB export TOOLB_HOME=/opt/toolB # <<< toolB <<<

p.example-tool-a-finds-one-ordered-pair: Tool A counts `<toolA>` / `</toolA>` and finds exactly one ordered pair: *present*, splice its body.

p.example-tool-b-markers-are-ordinary-host: Tool B's markers are, to tool A, ordinary host content — outside its block, therefore preserved verbatim.

p.example-tool-b-sees-the-mirror-image: Tool B sees the mirror image.

p.NEITHER-TOOL-NEEDS-TO-KNOW-THE-OTHER-EXI: Neither tool needs to know the other exists; the unique-marker requirement (§markers) is exactly what makes that independence hold.

p.THE-USERS-HAND-WRITTEN-CONTENT-SURVIVES-: The user's hand-written alias is outside both blocks and survives every operation of both tools.

p.MARKER-UNIQUENESS-PREVENTS-SILENT-MUTUAL: The failure this prevents is the reason marker uniqueness is not optional: if both tools used a generic `# BEGIN` / `# END`, each would match the other's block, and the second tool to run would splice its body into the first tool's region — silent mutual corruption.

re-derive.title: Re-derive for your project

p.this-document-states-the-practice-tool-n: This document states the practice tool-neutrally.

p.ADAPT-IT-BY-HANDING-YOUR-AGENT-THE-TASK: Adapt it by handing your agent the task, not a copied template:

re-derive.fence: Read this flow's documents (your project installed them — typically `vibedeps/flow-managed-blocks/<version>/spec/flows/managed-blocks/`, check `vibe.lock`) end to end. Then design the managed block for THIS tool: 1. Name the host files we write into and who else writes to each (the user by hand? other tools?). 2. Choose a unique, greppable, namespaced marker pair per file type, and write the exact byte-scan that locates them (no parser, no model). Include a version token in the opening marker. 3. Draft the do-not-edit notice that sits as the first line inside the block. 4. Restate the absent / present / malformed table in our terms, and write the exact hard-stop message for malformed. 5. Specify the three verbs, including that remove deletes the block AND its separation, and the byte-identical no-op. Show me the design before writing any code.

facts.SUM-A-WHOLE-FILE-REWRITE-IS-A-DATA-LOSS-: A whole-file rewrite of a shared file is a data-loss event. Own one delimited block; never touch a byte outside it.
facts.SUM-MARKER-PROPERTIES-AND-VERSIONING: Markers must be unique, greppable, paired, and carry an internal do-not-edit notice. Version the marker format from day one.
facts.SUM-THREE-STATES: Three states: absent → create at end of file; present → update or remove the body; malformed → hard stop, human decides.
facts.SUM-REMOVE-RESTORES-THE-FILE-AND-NO-OP-W: Remove deletes the block *and* its separation, restoring the file byte-for-byte. Never rewrite when the result is byte-identical.
facts.SUM-CLASSIFY-AT-PLAN-TIME: Classify at plan time so mutation never discovers a surprise.
facts.SUM-TWO-TOOLS-COHABIT-BECAUSE-MARKERS-AR: Two tools cohabit because each scans only for its own markers — which is why the markers must be unique.
